summary: Pass strict-function this exactly as supplied, including undefined, null, and primitives.

target.notes: The helper/calling convention must carry an explicit JS this value. It must not box primitives or substitute the global object.

caveats: C# instance methods always have a receiver and therefore are not a direct representation of arbitrary strict JS this.

tests.name: plain strict call gets undefined
tests.input: function f(){'use strict'; return this===undefined} console.log(f());

tests.name: strict call preserves primitive
tests.input: function f(){'use strict'; return this===2} console.log(f.call(2));
